findings.title: Service-Owner role-restriction obligation has no authorising PRD element
findings.description: Both lines impose a role-based access-control rule — a0ae: 'serve the request only to a caller bearing the Service-Owner role'; 3312: for a non-Service-Owner caller 'deny the request and return no counts'. The cited @prd: PRD.01.09.21ad is the 'Expose Counts' feature, whose sub-requirement PRD.01.09.e19e only requires counts be AVAILABLE to the Service Owner ('A Service Owner request returns both counts'); it establishes no authorization, role-check, or denial obligation. PRD-01 contains no access-control/auth element anywhere, and PRD §7 (line 154) explicitly lists 'user accounts and authentication' as out-of-scope. The @prd tag resolves syntactically (C4 OK) but the upstream element does not authorise the obligation it is attached to — an orphan/scope-creep enforcement rule that arguably contradicts the PRD scope boundary. Unlike c060/a132, neither line carries an [author assumption] deferral marker, so it is not an accepted deferral. Confirmed still present and unaddressed at iteration 5.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add an '[author assumption — no PRD access-control element]' note to both lines mirroring the c060 TLS treatment so the orphan is an explicit deferral; or (b) drop the role-restriction clause from a0ae and convert 3312 to a generic deferral leaving access control downstream; or (c) raise a PRD change adding an authorization constraint (§12) and re-point both @prd tags to it.

findings.title: Three conjoined obligations in one unwanted-behaviour line
findings.description: a2ae response is 'SHALL fail closed, issue no short code, and return [message]'; 9671 is 'SHALL reject the submission, issue no short code, and return [message]'. Each fuses three separately-testable obligations: (1) the fail-closed/reject decision, (2) the no-code-issued invariant, (3) the user-facing message string. A BDD author asserts these as distinct Then-clauses. The doc already split the takedown obligation into 539a (cease redirect) and 539b (not-found message) on exactly this atomicity principle, so the convention should apply here for internal consistency. One-rule-per-line atomicity is not met.
findings.recommendation: Split each into an outcome line (fail-closed/reject + no code issued, WITHIN 500 ms p95) and a separate message line, each carrying its own @prd tag, mirroring the 539a/539b split already applied.

findings.title: Throttling response not measurable / not enumerated
findings.description: Response is 'reject submit and redirect requests that exceed the configured rate with an explicit throttling response'. The numeric rate bound is correctly [ADR deferred], but the response SHAPE itself is unspecified — no status code (e.g. 429), no named user-facing message, and no WITHIN latency clause. Every sibling rejection line (eeaf, fa44, 0b67, a2ae, 9671) names a concrete user-facing message or a 5xx/explicit code; 'explicit throttling response' is verifiable only by product judgement, so a BDD author cannot assert the Then without inventing the response contract. Fails C3 measurability.
findings.recommendation: Name the throttling contract: an HTTP 429 (or a named throttling message) plus a WITHIN p95 clause, keeping only the numeric rate threshold as the [ADR deferred] value.

findings.title: Coupled secondary obligations folded into primary lines (idempotency rule; enforce+emit-event)
findings.description: Three lower-severity atomicity couplings. (a) f909's parenthetical '(Idempotency: identical-URL resubmission yields a new distinct code; no dedup.)' embeds an independently-testable normative rule (every resubmission yields a distinct code) into the shorten-response line, with no element ID and inheriting f909's tags. (b) ab5e ('throttle that source AND emit a detection event') and c7e3 ('apply the cooldown AND emit a detection event') each couple an enforcement obligation with a distinct observability obligation under one 100 ms budget; a system could satisfy one without the other, so they are separately verifiable. Lower priority than RS-002 because the enforce+emit and idempotency-side-effect idioms are conventionally compound, but they remain non-atomic.
findings.recommendation: Promote the f909 no-dedup rule to its own ubiquitous element with @prd: PRD.01.09.0999. For ab5e/c7e3, split the enforcement and detection-event obligations into separate lines, or reclassify each explicitly as a complex/compound requirement and state that both obligations share the 100 ms budget.

findings.location: EARS.01.04.c060 (§4 Security, lines 370, 376) and EARS.01.04.ca05 (§4 Reliability, lines 382, 387)
findings.title: Two §4 quality rows lack a PRD anchor (BRD-direct trace, self-disclosed)
findings.description: c060 (HTTPS/TLS 1.2+) traces only to @brd: BRD.01.10.c2e1 and self-discloses '[author assumption — no PRD transport-encryption element]'. ca05 (99.9% monthly availability) carries @brd: BRD.01.04.f439 + @threshold but no @prd tag; PRD §5 (lines 125-127) deliberately treats availability as a post-launch operational objective tracked upstream, not a PRD element. Both are C5 PRD-anchor gaps, but each is sanctioned by an explicit in-doc deferral/disclosure, so severity is low. Noted for completeness and to confirm the deferral markers remain present and correct at iteration 5.
findings.recommendation: Accept as-is given the explicit deferral markers; optionally add a PRD §12 transport-encryption constraint and a PRD §12 availability anchor so both §4 rows gain PRD anchors and the C5 gap closes cleanly.
